mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up our dive into Trick Mirror, you probably feel it too—the world Jia Tolentino describes is tangled, sometimes overwhelming, but there’s always a spark of hope hiding in the mess. This journey hasn’t been about simple solutions. It’s about learning to spot those invisible forces shaping our days—on screens and off. We’ve talked about the little ways we fool ourselves, the stories we inherit, and the roles we play, often without stopping to notice. But woven through it all? There’s the real possibility of change, the subtle strength of honesty, and the guts it takes to live in a new way. So, what can you take away from all this? The internet has a way of blurring who we truly are and who we pretend to be. The big stories—those cultural narratives—shape our choices more than we might ever admit. Self-delusion? It’s just part of being human, but it’s absolutely something we can work through. The words we use, the stories we tell—they can box us in, or open us up to new possibilities. And even in a world obsessed with spectacle, nothing beats the risk and reward of real, honest connection. Here’s what this means for you. You don’t have to be perfect to be real. That pressure to always perform, to curate every moment—it’s exhausting, isn’t it? It’s totally okay to step back. The best connections, the deepest sense of self, come from being known—not just being seen. If you ever find yourself stuck in that loop of self-doubt or second-guessing, remember—you’re not alone. Living honestly is a journey, not a finish line. There’s always time for a fresh start. Every small act of honesty, every moment of vulnerability, every time you question an old story—those are the things that open up new ways to live. The mirror might be tricky, but it’s never unbreakable. You have the power to see yourself, and the world, more clearly—one brave choice at a time.
